newsitem.title: FINLAND: Summit notebook- Low-fat dinner and low-key demos.
newsitem.headline: Summit notebook- Low-fat dinner and low-key demos.

text.p: Low-fat Finnish delicacies generally good for a man with heart problems -- consomme, fish and reindeer -- featured on the menu for the pre-summit supper in Helsinki's presidential palace.
Reindeer roam freely in Arctic northern Finland and scratch food from often frozen ground, keeping their meat very lean.

"It's a healthy menu: quite plain; but it includes the best ingredients Finland can offer at this time of year," said Jaakko Nuutila, chef at upmarket Helsinki restaurant Savoy. "The goose consomme will be the dish of the menu -- that's unusual."
Geese are farmed in Finland's southwestern islands.
Goose consomme flavoured with cep mushrooms
Cold-smoked salmon timbale with parsley sauce

A spattering of peaceful demonstrations included students from the former Soviet Baltic republics bidding for inclusion in the first wave of NATO expansion, anarchists and protesters reclaiming land Finland lost to the Soviet Union in World War Two.
About 30 Lithuanian students gathered outside the press centre Finlandia Hall, saying Lithuania's inclusion would bring "more stability and security to the Baltic sea region and the whole of Europe".
Police said they were holding an arson suspect after a fire broke out in a Russian strip club called Little St Petersburg in central Helsinki early on Thursday.
No one was injured and a spokesman said he did not see a link to either organised crime or the summit in the fire, caused by petrol.
